text.en: Meena saw a picture of Mohenjo-daro's great bath. "Cities this old?" she wondered.

Ancient civilisations grew along great rivers: Mesopotamia on the Tigris and Euphrates, Egypt on the Nile, the Indus Valley and China on the Yellow River. Rivers gave fertile land and water for farming and travel.
The Indus Valley civilisation had well-planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, with grid streets, drainage and a great bath. The Egyptians built pyramids and wrote in hieroglyphics, while Mesopotamians used cuneiform writing and the Chinese developed silk and the calendar.
These civilisations had trade, writing, art and organised government. They left behind monuments and artefacts that tell us how people lived.

problem.en: Why did early civilisations begin near rivers?

text.en: Rivers give water and fertile soil.

prompt.en: A friend says Harappan cities had no planning. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: They had grid streets and drains.
